How It Unfolds

Connection Happens In Stages

Unity Spark Project unfolds in four stages — each one building on the last, from seeing our neighbors to truly celebrating who we are together.

01
SEE
Hello Neighbor
Neighbor portraits displayed throughout the community. Trained interviewers and photographers capture the faces and stories of Puyallup residents — sharing them publicly so we can see and appreciate who lives here.
02
HEAR
Community Conversations
Farmer's Market pop-ups and outdoor gatherings, through October. Informal, open spaces where neighbors slow down, share a story, and find common ground with the person right next to them.
03
KNOW
Cultural Exchange Experiences
Facilitated gatherings that go deeper. Small groups come together across cultures and neighborhoods for storytelling, deep listening, and dialogue. This is where empathy takes root.
04
CELEBRATE
Multicultural Festival
A citywide Folklorama-inspired celebration — coming in a future year. Food, art, music, storytelling, and shared joy. Built on everything this pilot teaches us, designed to be annual and community-owned.

Why It Matters

This Is Not Just
a Program.

We are living in a time of deep division, disconnection, and isolation. But what if the solution isn't louder debate — it's deeper connection?

Stronger communities don't happen by accident. They are built through intentional relationships, shared understanding, and collective care.

It's a new model for how we live together.

"

This work cannot be automated or outsourced. It must be held by an organization rooted in trust, story, and humanity.

Unity Spark Project — Hello Puyallup Initiative Brief
Hello Puyallup

A Living Model for
Civic Belonging

Hello Puyallup is a mayor-led pilot that brings this vision to life — inviting neighbors to connect, listen, and build community together. Through storytelling, cultural exchange, and shared experiences, this initiative transforms neighborliness into a visible and powerful civic value.

Led by Unity Spark in partnership with the City of Puyallup, this pilot is intentionally designed from the outset to become a replicable national model for civic neighborliness.

Learn About the Pilot →
NOW
First
Hello Puyallup Public Art
Neighbor portraits go up throughout the community. Trained interviewers and photographers capture the faces and stories of Puyallup — displayed publicly for as long as possible so everyone can see who their neighbors really are.
NEXT
Then
Community Conversations
Informal gatherings at the Farmer's Market and outdoor pop-ups, running through October. Open to everyone — no registration required, just show up and say hello.
THEN
Ongoing
Cultural Exchange Experiences
Facilitated small-group gatherings across cultures and neighborhoods. Dates and number of events to be announced — follow along to stay in the loop.
2025+
Future
Multicultural Celebration
A citywide Folklorama-inspired celebration is being planned for a future year — designed to be annual, community-owned, and built on everything this pilot teaches us.

The MLK Day Celebration brought together neighbors from across the city — civic leaders, youth, cultural ambassadors, and everyday residents — for a morning of reflection, unity, and shared purpose. This is what the beloved community looks like when it gathers.
